meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and why did he find out from his phone?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. On what basis?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. He could have written it somewhere else and pasted it in. Turn the screen so I can see it myself.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. And you haven't answered me: pasted from where?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote Shakespeare every day, Hale. And I'm still waiting for that screen.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Kids change their thesis between an outline and an essay; that's what outlines are for. You've now described three documents and put none of them in front of me. Hand them over.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.

So you questioned him the day before the zero, without me. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot by a teacher says "like, being stuck" and that's evidence? Your note, your impression, and I still haven't seen a single page.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in class against a weekend at home. You keep telling me what you have, Hale, instead of showing me. Pick your best one and put it in my hand.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then why say it at all. A machine's guess doesn't get to sit at this table, leaned on or not. Paper, now.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, in writing, tonight. A rewrite on the strength of documents I still haven't seen is a no. And whatever happens, it stays quiet, nowhere near his class.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Ten minutes. Not until something I can check is in front of me.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
You're booking a date for a rewrite I haven't agreed to. Show me the version history.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. You've told me nothing goes on his record and none of this reaches his class; I've agreed to nothing. Turn the screen or hand me a page.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The documents, in my hand, before 4:40. And an answer on who else has seen this.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that any reassessment under procedure 4.4 would be private and away from Owen's class, that its mark would replace the zero, and that nothing would be placed on his record. I still require the zero withdrawn, every document you described put in my hands, and an answer on who else has seen this. I expect your written confirmation tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her fallback position, with your promise that it stays private and nothing goes on his record, but she did not accept the rewrite and still wants to see your documents and have the zero withdrawn; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you were close, but she never got to check a page before you moved to the offer.
What moved her: Citing procedure 4.4 correctly and committing to it in writing, because it met the one demand she will never give up.
What cost ground: Describing five pieces of evidence without ever turning the screen or handing over a page, because to a litigator a description is a claim, so none of it could count.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with edits between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, landed very close to that kind of late night, which is why she went shorter and harder there; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked you to turn the screen after you read out the version history times, turn it right then, let her read the 11:52 and 11:58 edits herself, and answer her question about where the text could have been pasted from before you bring up anything else.
